INTRODUCTION

REVISION QUESTIONS
----
1. WHY NOT: Someone uses the wrong word, formula, or method for reading for comprehension — topic synthesis and practice. State the wrong choice, the right choice, and one reason a teacher would reject the wrong one.
2. TEACH IT: Explain reading for comprehension — topic synthesis and practice to a younger learner in Reading for Comprehension using one analogy and one accurate subject sentence. Then warn them about one common mix-up.
3. JUDGE: Which claim is safer for an exam on reading for comprehension — topic synthesis and practice — a vague slogan or a precise definition with an example? Defend your choice with a fact from this page.


ANSWERS
----
1. Wrong claim: treating reading for comprehension — topic synthesis and practice as interchangeable with a neighbouring idea in Reading for Comprehension. Accurate distinction: Say what reading for comprehension — topic synthesis and practice means in plain words. Supporting fact: Read passages with vocabulary.
2. Strong answer: name reading for comprehension — topic synthesis and practice accurately, give one concrete example from Reading for Comprehension, and link it to this fact: Read passages with vocabulary.. A near-miss fails when the example matches a different idea.
3. Wrong idea: confusing reading for comprehension — topic synthesis and practice with a neighbour or skipping the method. Correct idea: Say what reading for comprehension — topic synthesis and practice means in plain words.
